title: Control flow
description: if, loops, switch, break, and continue

exercises.title: If Statement
exercises.description: Declare age = 20. If age >= 18, print Adult. Otherwise print Minor.
hints: `if (age >= 18) puts("Adult"); else puts("Minor");` — `puts` adds a trailing newline.

exercises.title: For Loop
exercises.description: Use a for loop to print numbers 1 through 5.

exercises.title: Switch Statement
exercises.description: Declare day = 2. Use a switch statement to print the day name: 1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, 3=Wednesday, default=Unknown.
hints: `switch (day) { ... }` with `case 2: puts("Tuesday"); break;` — use `break` unless fall-through is intentional.

exercises.title: For-Range Loop
exercises.description: Create a slice colors = list["red", "green", "blue"}. Use for ... in to print each color on its own line.
hints: `const char *colors[] = {...};` then `for (size_t i = 0; i < 3; i++) printf("%s\n", colors[i]);`

exercises.title: Else If Chain
exercises.description: Declare score = 85. Print the grade: 90+ = A, 80+ = B, 70+ = C, 60+ = D, below 60 = F.
hints: Chain `if / else if` from the highest band downward (`A` then `B` …).

exercises.title: For Loop with Break
exercises.description: Use a for loop to count from 1 upward. When i reaches 5, break out of the loop. Print each number before the break.
hints: With `for (;;)`, print `i`, then increment; `if (i >= 5) break;` stops before printing `5`.

exercises.title: Continue Statement
exercises.description: Use a for loop to print numbers 1 to 10, but skip printing even numbers using continue.
hints: Inside `for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++)`, skip evens with `if (i % 2 == 0) continue;`.
